label: v0.1
notes:
- This first build is the moves test: try every move together. The Postyard is still simple shapes; the next build brings the real open world.
- First test of Slingbound: two friends, two phones, one ribbon, with Spark and Crag as real 3D heroes.
- Invite a friend with a 5-letter code; on the same Wi-Fi the phones connect directly.
- The Postyard: six practice rings to explore together (welcome court, small roofs, return yard, catch arcade, counterweight tower, borrowed-tools garden), all open for this test.
- Walk, jump, brace, sling each other, catch in mid-air (with a second-chance catch), throw Crag like a cannonball, ride the counterweight, grab, carry, push, climb, hang, slide and ring the bells.
- Two control styles to compare (Pause > Controls): Classic with a Hold / Grab button, or one Action button with a quick, normal or slow hold.
- Little extras: pings to point the way, a fun move or a high five when you tap with nothing to do, "Start from scratch" (in Pause) to see the controls unlock one by one.
- A new woven ribbon, plus three other looks to try (Pause > Ribbon look).
- A side-view alley where lantern shadows become ledges, and an upright runner street that folds up behind you.
- Toys only here: distance sling board, bell course, catch the falling letters, parcel bowling and more.
- Known: online play outside the same Wi-Fi can feel slow for now (about a quarter of a second there and back from Riyadh in our test); same Wi-Fi is the smooth way to play.
- The small TEST mark in the corner of the play screen is on purpose (first test build).

label: v0.2
notes:
- The Postyard is now a real open world in the sky: pink-rock islands with mossy cliffs and waterfalls over a sea of clouds, linked by red stone arches, a rope-net sky bridge, cloth-ribbon bridges and timber bridges, with a rope net hung over the sling gap.
- Stone courts and streets to walk in: ivory and pink paving, walls with crenellations, arches and arcades, tile-roof houses with wooden balconies, market stalls, a shadow-puppet theatre, woven banners and awnings, palms, plants and lanterns.
- The counterweight tower is a tall earth-plaster tower with turning brass pulleys and red belts; the crane by the ring rig swings its hook and net.
- The toys court has rugs, a rug roller, a fountain and drums; the east yard has striped awnings and stepping posts.
- Blue sky, warm sun and soft shadows; the rope-net and cloth bridges sag a little under your steps; parcels and barrels stay put, bowling pins still fall.
- Spark is soft pink and furry again, with clear eyes that blink.
- The side alley and the runner street are dressed in the same stone, brass and cloth.
- Should be fixed: the game could crash when both players tapped Ready in the room and the world started.
- Should be fixed: a crash on Android after leaving a lobby and joining it again.
- After both tap Ready, a loading screen (three dots) builds the world for both phones together.
- In the runner street you now see your partner duck on your own phone.
- A raised terrace with a curved stair in the main court, under a shade sail.
- Fall off an island and you come back right where you last stood.
- Bigger letter keys on the join screen.
- The Classic controls now show a Hold / Grab label on screen.
- Arabic: clearer words for "local network is off" and for the ring button.
- Known: online play outside the same Wi-Fi can still feel slow; same Wi-Fi is the smooth way to play.
- Known: Arabic lines that talk about your partner do not use the female form yet.
- Known: the invite link opens the studio page, not the game yet: type the 5-letter code on the Join screen.
- Known: this test is Android only; iPhone comes in a later test.
- Known: two phones on the same Wi-Fi was tested as two copies of the game talking over the network, not yet on two real phones: tell us how your game goes.
- Known: some wide views of the world are heavier to draw than we want; tell us if any place stutters on your phone.
- Known: the first time the world builds after you both tap Ready it can take a minute or more on a phone; it is faster the next time.
- Known: how smooth online play is on real phones is measured from your games in this test.

label: v0.3
notes:
- One clear job: carry the parcel to the glowing Post Tower through five stations. Each one opens only when you solve it together: the gate (both stand on the two pads), the low wall (climb the ladder), the gap (brace and sling your partner, then they kick down a plank for you), the high ledge (sling one up to pull the lever, a ladder drops for the other) and the delivery at the tower.
- A see-through pair shows each station's move once when you arrive, and again if you are stuck. Each station gives a stamp on your postcard (top left) with a stamp sound; five stamps and the parcel in the tower box = "Delivered!".
- After the delivery the whole Postyard is free to explore. From the menu you can restart the path or jump to any station.
- Slinging is now simple: posts are no longer anchors, only your partner is. Your partner holds ACTION to brace (you see their glow and feel a buzz), then you alone pull and aim. A short pull lands near, a full pull goes 14 m, and you land exactly where the thick white line and ring show. The camera rises behind you while you aim and stays still.
- A calm camera: it follows smoothly, keeps both heroes in view and only turns behind you while you run straight ahead. It moves in close at walls so it never hides inside one, and finds your partner again if a wall is in the way. The standing plank at the gap steps out of the picture while it hides you. Tap the small recenter button to bring it behind you. The lock button is gone.
- The heroes move a bit slower, speed up and stop smoothly and turn in a curve. You can't drift far apart (about 8 m); a sling stretches further, then the ribbon pulls back.
- Spark is quicker and hops higher; Crag is heavier and lands with a thump.
- Only two big buttons: JUMP and ACTION (its picture shows what it will do). Ping: press the ping button, drag to the spot and let go.
- Things that look solid are solid now: walls, crates, carts, houses and railings block you; grass, flowers and cloth you brush through.
- Same Wi-Fi: both tap "Same Wi-Fi" on the home screen, tap your friend's card, they say yes, and you are in the room together, even with no internet. A small light shows how good the connection is, and Ready waits until the link is steady.
- The world builds faster after you both tap Ready, with a bar that really moves, and the connection holds while it loads.
- Known: the start is much faster but not yet measured on a real phone; tell us if it takes longer than half a minute or the picture freezes.
- Known: Same Wi-Fi was tested on one computer, not yet on two real phones; tell us how it goes.
- Known: the small striped flask tag on the play screen is on purpose: this is a test build, and after "Delivered!" every place of the Postyard is open.
- Known: some Arabic lines that name your friend still use the male form.
- Known: this test is Android only.
